transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what’s been troubling you or what brings you in today?

Hi, yeah... um, thanks for seeing me. I just... I don't even really know where to start, honestly, because it's just taking over my whole life right now. It's my face. Well, specifically, the left side of my face. It's just completely crooked and... and messed up. 

I mean, I look in the mirror before my shift—I work as an order filler at this massive distribution warehouse, right? So there are all these bright, terrible fluorescent lights everywhere, bouncing off the concrete floors. And I'm stocking shelves, trying to just do my job, but I can just feel people looking at me. Like the other guys on the floor, or the supervisors when they walk by. I just know they're staring at how asymmetrical and weird the left side of my face looks. 

And it's not just at work, either. I used to really love going to salsa night on Thursdays. It was my thing, you know? A good way to unwind after hauling boxes all week. But lately, I can't even focus on the steps or the music because I'm so hyper-aware of my face. I spend the whole night trying to turn my head so my dance partners only see my right side, which is exhausting, and I just know they're noticing how crooked I am anyway. I ask my friends about it, I ask my buddies at the warehouse, and they all swear they don't see anything. They tell me I look fine, but I know they're just being polite or they just don't want to make me feel bad, right? Because I can see it. And I just can't stop thinking about it. From the second I wake up to when I go to sleep, it's just... it's all I think about. It's literally all I can focus on.
Do you find yourself doing anything repeatedly—like checking mirrors, touching your face, or trying to fix or hide the way your face looks—to try to deal with the discomfort you feel?

Yeah... yeah, I definitely do that. I mean, it's basically constant. It's like I can't stop myself, even when I know I need to be doing something else. Especially at work. Like, we get these fifteen-minute breaks, right? And I'm supposed to be resting my legs or grabbing a drink, but instead, I end up practically sprinting to the bathroom. And the lighting in there is just... it's brutal. It's this harsh, flickering fluorescent thing that just highlights every single flaw, every shadow on the left side of my face. 

So I stand there, and I just stare. I check the mirror from the front, then I turn to the side, then I turn back, trying to see if maybe it doesn't look as bad as I thought, but it always does. And I catch myself touching it, too. I'll rub at this one specific spot on my cheek, right where it looks the most uneven, like maybe if I press on it enough, it'll just... I don't know, flatten out or look normal. I do it so much the skin gets all red and irritated, which probably just makes it look worse, honestly. 

And then I try to fix my baseball cap. We have to wear these company hats, and I'll spend God knows how long pulling the brim down low on the left side, adjusting it a fraction of an inch, taking it off, putting it back on, trying to cast a shadow over that part of my face so nobody else can see how crooked it is when I go back out on the floor. 

The problem is, I get so caught up in doing all of this—checking, rubbing, adjusting the hat—that I completely lose track of time. A fifteen-minute break turns into twenty, twenty-five minutes. And in a warehouse, they track everything. They have these scanners that monitor our pick rates, how many items we're pulling per hour. And because I'm stuck in the bathroom trying to fix my face, my picking numbers just tank. I fall so far behind. My supervisor, Dave—he's this real hard-ass guy—he's been getting on my case about it constantly lately. He's always pulling me aside, asking why my numbers are dropping, why I'm taking so long on my breaks. And I can't exactly tell him, "Oh, sorry Dave, I was busy staring at my deformed face in the mirror for twenty minutes." So I just make up excuses, but I know he's getting fed up, and I'm terrified I'm going to lose my job over this, but I just... I can't stop doing it. I have to check. I have to try and hide it.
Do these behaviors or thoughts about your face ever feel like they’re outside of your control, or do you ever feel anxious or distressed if you try to stop them?

Yeah, absolutely. It's... it's completely out of my control. Like, I'll tell myself, "Okay, this break, I'm just going to sit in the breakroom, drink my water, and look at my phone. I'm not going to the bathroom." I'll literally repeat it in my head while I'm walking off the floor. But then this... this feeling starts creeping up. It's like this tight, heavy knot right in the center of my chest, and my heart starts beating faster, and my palms get all sweaty. And all I can think is, "What if my hat shifted? What if the lighting out here makes it look even worse? I just need to check real quick. Just one look to make sure it's not as bad as I think."

And if I try to just sit there and ignore it? It's impossible. The anxiety just builds and builds until I feel like I'm going to jump out of my skin. I start getting fidgety, tapping my foot, and I can't even focus on whatever I'm trying to look at on my phone. It's like my brain is screaming at me that everyone is looking at my crooked face and I have to go fix it right now. So I always cave. I always end up practically running to the bathroom anyway, because the relief of just... checking, even if it makes me feel terrible because I still look messed up, is better than that overwhelming panic of not knowing. 

And it's the same with the rubbing. I'll be on the floor, scanning boxes, and I'll realize my hand is on my cheek again, pressing into that spot. I'll pull my hand away and tell myself to stop, but five minutes later, without even realizing I did it, my hand is right back up there. It's like a reflex at this point. I just... I can't stop it, no matter how hard I try or how much trouble it gets me into with Dave. It just feels like this compulsion that totally overrides my own willpower, you know?
Have you ever had any experiences where you felt like your thoughts weren't your own, or that someone else was controlling your actions, or that you were being watched or followed?

No, no, nothing like that at all. I mean, my thoughts are definitely my own. Honestly, that’s almost the worst part of all this, you know? It’s all me. It’s my own brain just running a million miles an hour, constantly replaying how bad I look. Sometimes I actually wish someone else *was* controlling my actions, because then maybe they’d make me stop rubbing my cheek or stop running to the warehouse bathroom every ten minutes! But no, it’s just me. I know it’s my own self telling me to go check the mirror, even when I know it's going to get me in trouble with Dave. It's like a broken record in my own head, but it's definitely my head. 

And as for being watched or followed... I mean, when I said earlier that I feel like people are looking at me, I just mean regular people, like the guys on the floor or the people at salsa night. I know they're staring at my face because the left side is so crooked and uneven. But I don't think I'm being, like, stalked or followed by anyone in a creepy way. It's not like there are hidden cameras in my apartment or someone is tracking my truck or anything crazy like that. It's strictly just... I know people notice how messed up my face is when I'm out in public or under those awful fluorescent lights. But when I'm home alone, I know I'm alone. Nobody is putting thoughts into my head or pulling my strings. It’s really just my own mind driving me absolutely crazy all day long.
